title: Name the Weekday of Any Date (Doomsday Method)
subject: math

sections.body: The mathematician John Conway invented a way to find the weekday of any date in your head. It uses the 'doomsday' of a year: a weekday that many easy-to-remember dates share. This lesson covers the years 2000 to 2099.

The doomsday dates in any year all fall on the same weekday: 4 April, 6 June, 8 August, 10 October and 12 December (4/4, 6/6, 8/8, 10/10, 12/12); and 9 May and 5 September, 11 July and 7 November (the pairs 9-5 and 7-11); and 14 March (Pi day, 3/14). In February, use the last day: 28 February, or 29 in a leap year. In January use 3 January, or 4 January in a leap year.

How to find the doomsday of a year from 2000 to 2099. Take the last two digits, y. Step 1: divide y by 12 and write the whole number part, a. Step 2: write the remainder, b. Step 3: divide b by 4 and write the whole number part, c. Add a + b + c. Count that many days on from Tuesday (the doomsday of 2000). Dropping whole weeks of 7 first makes this easier.

Example, 2023. y = 23. 23 ÷ 12 = 1 remainder 11, so a = 1 and b = 11. 11 ÷ 4 = 2 (whole part), so c = 2. a + b + c = 14, which is 2 whole weeks, leaving 0. So the doomsday of 2023 is Tuesday. Check: 4 April 2023 was a Tuesday.

Example, 2024. y = 24. a = 2, b = 0, c = 0. Total 2. Two days on from Tuesday is Thursday. Doomsday 2024 is Thursday. So 8 August 2024 was a Thursday. To find 12 August 2024, count 4 days on from Thursday: Friday, Saturday, Sunday, Monday. It was a Monday.
Find the doomsday of the current year. Then name the weekday of your birthday this year. Check with a calendar.

Every worked example here was checked with a computer for all years 2000 to 2099. The method needs practice, so start by remembering the pairs 4/4, 6/6, 8/8, 10/10, 12/12, then add the rest slowly. A later lesson extends the method to other centuries.

quiz.q: Which date always falls on the same weekday as 6 June in the same year?
hints: Think of the doomsday dates: pairs of matching numbers.
6/6 is one. Which date here is also a matching pair, like 4/4 or 10/10?
Example: 4 April and 10 October share a weekday in every year, as do 12 December. Which one here is a matching pair?
quiz.explain: 8/8 is a doomsday date, so 8 August has the same weekday as 6 June.

quiz.q: The doomsday of 2024 is Thursday. What weekday was 8 August 2024?
hints: Yes, 8/8 is one. Doomsday dates share the weekday of the doomsday.
Example: 2023's doomsday is Tuesday, so 4 April 2023 was a Tuesday, because 4/4 is a doomsday date. Use the same idea for 8/8.
quiz.explain: 8/8 is a doomsday date, so it falls on the doomsday weekday, Thursday.

quiz.q: The doomsday of 2024 is Thursday. What weekday was 12 August 2024?
hints: Start from the nearest doomsday date in the same month.
8 August is a doomsday date, so it was a Thursday. Count on 4 days to reach 12 August.
Example: 2023's doomsday is Tuesday. 6 June is a doomsday date, so 10 June is 4 days on: a Saturday. Count on from 8 August in the same way.
quiz.explain: 8 August 2024 was a Thursday. 4 days on: Friday, Saturday, Sunday, Monday.
